constrained_WER_estimate.basis: scaling the 12.17 -> 5.68 offline/LLM ratio in arXiv:2507.02800 onto this project's ~2.7% unconstrained full-stack figure

unconstrained_WER_reference.status: UNVERIFIED - only a 1-gram LM is present locally

scoring.note: Candidates whose value is validity, control or latency rather than accuracy score at or below zero by construction; see their tags.

candidates.name: Build a pruned/quantized 4-gram LM that fits 32 GB
candidates.mechanism: Build a custom KenLM 4-gram with aggressive pruning and quantization, compiled to a TLG WFST. The 7th-place B2T'25 entry reports doing exactly this at 19 GB RAM, down from the 300 GB unpruned 5-gram, trained on 80% general text + 20% conversational.
candidates.source: 7th-place B2T'25 writeup (medium.com/@jackson3b04); repo README (3-gram ~60 GB, 5-gram ~300 GB)

dper.reasoning: Acoustic model untouched.

dwer.reasoning: Measured against the 1-gram that is the only artifact present locally. n-gram order is the largest single lever in the LM stack; arXiv:2507.02800 shows 3-gram -> 5-gram worth 12.17 -> 8.18 WER (4 pts) on the sibling benchmark. Conservative because that is a different participant and LM corpus.

latency.L_comp: beam search cost grows with graph size; UNMEASURED

candidates.memory: 19 GB inference RAM (fits 32 GB with the 131 MB acoustic model)

risk.failure_mode: LM build toolchain (SRILM/KenLM + OpenFST) is fiddly; RAM during compilation can exceed the deployment target even if the artifact fits.

candidates.confounds: Changes the optimal acoustic_scale - re-run lm_param_sweep afterwards.
candidates.kill_criterion: Best artifact under 32 GB fails to beat the 1-gram by >1 WER pt.

candidates.name: Adaptive-compute decoding gated on n-gram confidence (S5)
candidates.mechanism: Always run the cheap incremental path; invoke expensive rescoring only when the n-gram hypothesis confidence falls below a threshold. Sweeping the threshold produces a genuine expected-latency vs accuracy curve - the deliverable the project currently lacks. Gate on LM score spread, NOT acoustic entropy: only 2.9% of frames exceed entropy 0.5 and the model is confidently wrong rather than uncertain (BUDGET 4).
candidates.source: Reviewer prior S5; the 7th-place B2T'25 entry already ships a version (n-gram confidence gate at -3.76)

dper.reasoning: Acoustic model untouched.

dwer.reasoning: Upper-bounded by full rescoring's gain; realized fraction depends on how well the gate identifies the utterances rescoring would have fixed. Reports EXPECTED latency, so worst-case still violates the budget - state that explicitly.

latency.L_comp: expected +5-50 ms; worst case still 620-830 ms

candidates.memory: depends on the escalation path (up to 12.4 GB VRAM if OPT is the fallback)

risk.failure_mode: Reports an expected latency against a HARD constraint. A reviewer can reasonably reject expected-case latency for a real-time claim.

candidates.confounds: Requires incremental_baseline and a working rescorer first.
candidates.kill_criterion: Gate cannot reach 80% of full-rescore gain at <25% trigger rate.

candidates.name: Small causal neural LM via shallow fusion
candidates.mechanism: Replace end-of-utterance OPT-6.7B rescoring with shallow fusion of a small causal LM (100-500 M params) scored incrementally during beam search. Because it is causal and scores token-by-token, it adds bounded per-frame cost instead of an end-of-utterance wall.
candidates.source: Standard streaming-ASR shallow fusion; motivated by BUDGET 1 (OPT is a 620-830 ms batch wall)

dper.reasoning: Acoustic model untouched.

dwer.reasoning: Recovers part of the gap between n-gram-only and LLM-rescored decoding. arXiv:2507.02800 shows LLM rescoring worth 12.17 -> 5.68 (53% relative); shallow fusion with a much smaller causal LM typically captures a third to a half of that.

latency.L_comp: +2-10 ms per emitted word (estimated); fits the ~79 ms slack

risk.failure_mode: Tokenizer mismatch between the WFST word lexicon and a subword LM; fusion weight needs its own sweep.

candidates.confounds: Do not bundle with ngram_4gram - both change the LM score scale.
candidates.kill_criterion: Cannot beat a same-RAM larger n-gram at equal latency.

candidates.name: Incremental LLM rescoring over a rolling context
candidates.mechanism: Instead of rescoring complete sentences at end-of-utterance, rescore a rolling window of the partial hypothesis with hypothesis pruning, updating as words stabilize. Amortizes the LLM cost across the utterance rather than paying it in one block.
candidates.source: Novel for this project; standard incremental-NLU pattern

dper.reasoning: Acoustic model untouched.

dwer.reasoning: Aims to recover most of full LLM rescoring. Discounted because rescoring a partial hypothesis is strictly weaker than rescoring a complete one - the LLM's advantage is largely right-context, which a streaming system does not have.

latency.L_comp: +10-40 ms per stabilized word (estimated)

candidates.memory: 12.4 GB VRAM for OPT-6.7B; less for a smaller rescorer

risk.failure_mode: Repeated partial rescoring can thrash: each update may revise earlier words, directly worsening the stability metric this project is trying to own.

candidates.confounds: Interacts with endpointing and with the stability metric.
candidates.kill_criterion: Flicker rate exceeds 0.5 revisions/word, or latency exceeds 79 ms at p95.

candidates.name: Lightweight test-time adaptation (DietCORP-style)
candidates.mechanism: At test time, build Z augmented copies of the current trial (time masking, white noise, baseline shift), take ONE gradient step updating only the patch-embedding module, then decode. The source paper measures 18.21 +/- 5.34 ms per trial at 1.33 GiB - which fits comfortably inside this project's ~79 ms of unspent budget.
candidates.source: arXiv:2507.02800 (DietCORP variant); contributes to their >20% WER reduction

dper.reasoning: Directly targets the inter-session degradation that arXiv:2605.24313 identifies as the dominant source of variability on this data. Requires NO training run - it adapts the released checkpoint.

dwer.reasoning: Their gain is entangled with time masking and the transformer; the TTA-only component is UNCERTAIN.

latency.L_comp: +18.21 +/- 5.34 ms per trial (measured in source paper)

risk.failure_mode: A gradient step at inference breaks the streaming-equivalence guarantee and makes the decoder non-deterministic across runs. Also: is it per-trial (fits) or per-frame (does not)? Per-trial only.

candidates.confounds: Adapting mid-utterance would change earlier frames' interpretation; adapt only at utterance boundaries.
candidates.kill_criterion: No WER improvement on held-out sessions, or per-trial cost exceeds 40 ms.

candidates.name: Online day-layer adaptation
candidates.mechanism: Update only the day-specific affine layer online during a session using an unsupervised objective (e.g. entropy minimization on the decoder's own output), leaving the GRU frozen.
candidates.source: Novel for this project; related to arXiv:2507.02800's TTA

dper.reasoning: The day layer is 262,656 parameters and is the designated locus of session variation, so it is the natural adaptation target. SCOPE NOTE: the brief excludes calibration-efficiency work; this is online adaptation during use, not calibration reduction, but the boundary is thin and should be confirmed.

latency.L_comp: +~1 ms per update if updates are sparse

risk.failure_mode: Entropy minimization on an ALREADY over-confident posterior (mean entropy 0.9% of max) has almost no gradient signal - this specific objective is likely to no-op on this model.

candidates.confounds: Interacts with label_smoothing, which changes the entropy the objective keys on.
candidates.kill_criterion: Adaptation moves val PER by <0.05 pts, consistent with a vanishing entropy gradient.

candidates.name: Beam / acoustic-scale / blank-penalty sweep on cached logits
candidates.mechanism: Sweep acoustic_scale, blank_penalty, beam, max_active and nbest against the already-saved validation logits, so the acoustic model never re-runs. The repo's own two configurations disagree by 10x on blank_penalty (code default 9.0 at language-model-standalone.py:809 vs README recipe 90) and differ on acoustic_scale (0.3 vs 0.325), which is direct evidence that neither was tuned for this checkpoint.
candidates.source: Repo defaults vs README recipe; standard WFST practice

dper.reasoning: Acoustic model untouched; PER cannot change.

dwer.reasoning: Decode hyperparameters typically move WER 0.3-1.0 pts when previously untuned. Amplified here because the posterior is near one-hot (BUDGET 4), so the acoustic_scale that balances it against the LM is far from a default.

latency.L_comp: 0 (offline sweep); chosen point may change beam cost

risk.failure_mode: Overfitting the val split if swept too finely; hold out sessions.

candidates.confounds: Must be re-run after ANY change to the acoustic model or the LM artifact.
candidates.kill_criterion: Best swept point is within 0.1 WER pts of current defaults.

candidates.name: Phase-staggered replicas for sub-cadence resolution (S3)
candidates.mechanism: Evaluate the model at K=4 patch phase offsets {0,20,40,60} ms and merge, producing a collective emission grid at 20 ms instead of 80 ms. This simultaneously cuts L_buf and acts as a test-time-augmentation ensemble. AUDIT F10 finds random_cut=3 already exposes training to 3 of the 4 phases, and the smoother (FIR) and day layer (per-bin) are phase-agnostic, so ONE trained model probably suffices - no retrain.
candidates.source: Reviewer prior S3; mechanism is TTA, which bioRxiv 2026.06.02.729705 independently validates as 'pseudoensembling' with a single base decoder

dper.reasoning: TTA over a nuisance variable the model was already partly trained against. Modest but real, and it is measurable in ~30 min from the existing checkpoint with no training.

dwer.reasoning: Two independent effects: TTA smoothing of the posterior, plus 4x finer emission grid giving the LM more evidence per unit time. UNCERTAIN which dominates.

latency.L_comp: 4x forwards, batched: measured 7.4 ms at batch=4 on CPU, ~0.4 ms on GPU

risk.failure_mode: If the patch embedding turns out to be phase-sensitive despite random_cut, the 4 phases disagree and merging degrades accuracy. This is cheap to test first and the test is the deciding experiment.

candidates.confounds: Reports both a latency AND an accuracy change; must be evaluated on both axes or the accuracy delta will be misread as free.
candidates.kill_criterion: Per-phase greedy PER varies by >0.5 pts across the 4 phases, indicating phase sensitivity that a single model cannot serve.

candidates.name: Time masking (SpecAugment-style) with learnable MASK token
candidates.mechanism: Mask contiguous temporal spans of the input during training and replace them with a learnable MASK embedding. arXiv:2507.02800 masks ~53% of every trial (N=20 spans, max length 0.075 of the trial, start and duration uniform, overlap allowed). This repo currently has NO time masking of any kind.
candidates.source: arXiv:2507.02800 (Feghhi et al., rev 2025-11-02): 20-26% relative WER improvement

dper.reasoning: Their headline is WER on a different participant. Discounted heavily to PER because PER is closer to the acoustic model and the LM absorbs some of the gain. The prior is strong: it is the largest single regularizer in the closest published causal result, and AUDIT A2 shows this repo has only two additive-noise augmentations.

dwer.reasoning: PER->WER transfer UNCERTAIN and probably sublinear here, because the LM already repairs many phoneme errors. Range widened accordingly.

latency.L_comp: 0 (training-time only)

candidates.memory: negligible; may reduce VRAM via shorter effective sequences

risk.failure_mode: Masking so aggressively that CTC input length falls below target length -> infinite loss, and zero_infinity=False (rnn_trainer.py:242) turns that into a hard crash. Set zero_infinity=True first.

candidates.confounds: Must not be bundled with channel_masking or the augmentation sweep.
candidates.kill_criterion: No val PER improvement at any mask fraction in {25%, 50%, 65%} over 2 seeds.

candidates.name: Channel / electrode masking
candidates.mechanism: Randomly zero (or replace with a learned token) a subset of the 512 feature channels per trial during training - the frequency-axis analogue of SpecAugment, adapted to electrodes. Directly targets electrode drift and dropout, which is the dominant non-stationarity in chronic intracortical recordings.
candidates.source: SpecAugment analogue; motivated by AUDIT A2 (absent) and by inter-session degradation reported in arXiv:2605.24313

dper.reasoning: Smaller prior than time masking because the day-specific affine layers already absorb some channel-level variation, but nothing in the pipeline currently forces robustness to losing individual electrodes.

latency.L_comp: 0 (training-time only)

risk.failure_mode: Masking channels after the day layer instead of before would defeat the point.

candidates.confounds: Must not be bundled with time_masking.
candidates.kill_criterion: No val PER improvement at mask rates {5%, 10%, 20%}.

candidates.name: Causal transformer encoder (time-masked, compact)
candidates.mechanism: Replace the 5x768 GRU with 5 transformer blocks at d=384, 6 heads, unidirectional causal attention and T5 relative positions - 9.4 M parameters against the GRU's 56.7 M in the source paper. Trained with heavy time masking, this beat the unidirectional GRU by 20-26% relative WER and matched bidirectional SOTA.

dper.reasoning: Strongest architectural evidence available, and it is causal by construction. Discounted because it is a different participant (T12, area 6v), a different benchmark, and because their gain is entangled with time masking - which is separately available here at a fraction of the cost.

dwer.reasoning: Their 20-26% relative on a ~12% baseline; scaled to this project's lower baseline with wide uncertainty. UNCERTAIN.

latency.L_comp: 43% fewer MFLOPs than the GRU in the source paper; still launch-bound

candidates.memory: training VRAM 2.66 GiB vs 5.55 GiB (source paper); inference far smaller than 131 MB

risk.failure_mode: A new architecture in this codebase means the streaming-equivalence gate, the day-layer plumbing and the patcher all need re-derivation. Attention over a growing context needs explicit KV caching to stay O(1)/frame.

candidates.confounds: Their result bundles architecture with time masking. Run time_masking on the GRU FIRST to attribute correctly - otherwise this candidate takes credit for the cheap change.
candidates.kill_criterion: Does not match the GRU baseline within 0.3 PER pts after equal tuning budget.

candidates.name: Snapshot ensemble from a single cyclic-LR run
candidates.mechanism: Replace the single cosine decay with cyclic restarts and keep the model at each cycle minimum, yielding several diverse members from ONE training run.
candidates.source: Huang et al. snapshot ensembles

dper.reasoning: Snapshot members are less diverse than independently seeded ones, so expect roughly half to two-thirds of a true N=3 ensemble's gain - at one third of the cost.

latency.L_comp: same as an N-member ensemble at inference

risk.failure_mode: Cyclic restarts change the LR schedule, confounding this with the optimizer sweep. Final-cycle quality may fall below the cosine baseline.

candidates.confounds: Changes the LR schedule - must not be bundled with optimizer_sweep.
candidates.kill_criterion: Snapshot ensemble does not beat the single cosine-trained model by >0.15 WER pts.

candidates.name: Intermediate / self-conditioned CTC with feedback
candidates.mechanism: Attach auxiliary CTC heads after intermediate GRU layers, then project their phoneme posteriors back into the hidden state before the next block. This conditions deeper layers on the shallow layers' predictions, partially relaxing CTC's conditional-independence assumption. Nothing about it requires future context.
candidates.source: J. Neural Eng. 23(4) 2026 (hierarchical CTC, 10.1088/1741-2552/ae8576); Nozaki & Komatsu self-conditioned CTC

dper.reasoning: The source paper's hierarchical CTC contributes measurably on top of joint training (T12: 17.6% plain -> 16.1% hierarchical, a 1.5 pt gain). Discounted for T15, where all their gains were smaller, and for their bidirectional 2048-wide setting.

latency.L_comp: +~2 MFLOP/frame for the aux heads; inference can drop them entirely

risk.failure_mode: Auxiliary loss weight needs tuning; too high and the shallow layers over-commit to phoneme decisions the deep layers cannot revise.

candidates.confounds: Must NOT be bundled with cross_dataset_t12.
candidates.kill_criterion: No PER improvement at aux weights {0.1, 0.3, 0.5}.

candidates.name: Calibration: label smoothing / entropy regularization on CTC
candidates.mechanism: Add an entropy bonus or label-smoothing term to the CTC objective so the acoustic posterior stops collapsing to one-hot. Measured on causal_la0: mean posterior entropy is 0.033 nats against a maximum of 3.714 - 0.9% of maximum, with a numerically one-hot median frame. A near-one-hot posterior gives the beam search almost no acoustic alternatives, so the LM must overcome a ~1.0 posterior to fix an acoustic error.
candidates.source: Novel for this project - proposed from the BUDGET 4 measurement, not from the literature

dper.reasoning: Greedy PER may WORSEN slightly, since smoothing trades argmax sharpness for calibration. This candidate is not about PER.

dwer.reasoning: The gain is expected in the LM stage: a wider n-best list gives the LM more to work with. PER->WER transfer here is expected to be NEGATIVE-to-positive - the rare case where PER and WER should move in opposite directions. That makes it a clean test of whether PER is the right proxy at all.

risk.failure_mode: Over-smoothing flattens the posterior enough that blank skipping stops firing, silently raising LM cost.

candidates.confounds: Must be evaluated on WER, not PER. Re-run lm_param_sweep afterwards - the optimal acoustic_scale WILL move.
candidates.kill_criterion: WER does not improve at smoothing in {0.05, 0.1} after re-sweeping acoustic_scale.

candidates.name: Cross-dataset pretraining on Willett T12 with day+dataset affine
candidates.mechanism: Train jointly on Willett-2023 (T12) and Card-2024 (T15) using per-day AND per-dataset affine input transforms to align both participants into a shared latent space, then evaluate on T15. Adds roughly an order of magnitude more neural data at zero inference cost.

dper.reasoning: Their measured T15 gain is 1.1 PER pts, but that is confounded with their hierarchical CTC and a bidirectional 2048-wide GRU. The authors explicitly note joint training helps T12 far more than T15, so the pretraining-only component is discounted.

dwer.reasoning: They report 0.67 WER pts on T15; PER->WER transfer looks sublinear.

latency.L_comp: 0 (inference uses one dataset's affine only)

candidates.memory: +T12 dataset on disk; training VRAM unchanged

risk.failure_mode: T12 has a different electrode count and feature layout; the affine alignment is where this fails silently rather than loudly.

candidates.confounds: Must NOT be bundled with intermediate_ctc - the source paper changes both at once, which is exactly why its T15 attribution is ambiguous.
candidates.kill_criterion: T15 val PER does not improve by >0.2 pts after joint training with matched schedule.

candidates.name: Stochastic depth / drop-path across GRU layers
candidates.mechanism: Randomly skip whole GRU layers during training with a per-layer survival probability, so the network learns an implicit ensemble of depths. The 7th-place B2T'25 entry used drop-path together with heavy dropout and weight decay 0.005.
candidates.source: 7th-place B2T'25 writeup; Huang et al. stochastic depth

dper.reasoning: Modest prior. rnn_dropout=0.4 is already substantial, so the marginal regularization from drop-path is likely small.

latency.L_comp: 0 (train-time only; inference uses all layers)

risk.failure_mode: Skipping a GRU layer means passing the hidden state through unchanged, which requires matching widths - satisfied here (all layers 768).

candidates.confounds: Must not be bundled with dropout-rate changes.
candidates.kill_criterion: No PER improvement at survival probabilities {0.9, 0.8}.

candidates.name: Auxiliary diphone objective
candidates.mechanism: Add a second CTC head predicting context-dependent diphones alongside the phoneme head, sharing the encoder. Diphones capture coarticulation that monophone targets discard; the head is dropped at inference so latency is unchanged.
candidates.source: arXiv:2412.17227 names diphones as one of two training changes that helped; 1st-place B2T'24 used them; arXiv:2507.02800 reports diphone+GRU at 8.39% WER

dper.reasoning: Credited by the organizers' retrospective, but that was in a bidirectional, unconstrained setting and the reported diphone GRU (8.39%) did not beat the plain time-masked causal transformer (8.18%).

latency.L_comp: 0 at inference (aux head dropped)

candidates.memory: 39^2 = 1,521 classes before pruning -> 768x1521 = 1.2 M extra training params

risk.failure_mode: Diphone class count explodes and most classes are unobserved; needs frequency pruning or the aux CTC becomes degenerate.

candidates.confounds: Must not be bundled with intermediate_ctc - both add auxiliary CTC heads.
candidates.kill_criterion: No PER improvement at aux weights {0.1, 0.3} with a pruned diphone inventory.

candidates.name: Deep ensemble, N=3, batched logit averaging
candidates.mechanism: Train 3 independently seeded causal models, run them phase-aligned as a single batch dimension, and average logits before the beam search. Compute is settled: measured 7.4 ms at batch=4 on CPU - 9.3% of the 80 ms window - with zero added algorithmic latency.
candidates.source: arXiv:2412.17227 (all top-3 entrants ensembled); bioRxiv 2026.06.02.729705 (33.7% -> 26.0% closed-loop)

dper.reasoning: Ensembling reliably delivers, but the published magnitude was measured at a 33.7% baseline WER - 12x this project's operating point. Gains compress sharply as baseline error falls. Discounted hard, and N=3 captures most of the diminishing-returns curve.

dwer.reasoning: Logit averaging before the LM helps most where the acoustic model is uncertain; the near-one-hot posterior (BUDGET 4) means members may be highly correlated, further compressing the gain. UNCERTAIN.

latency.L_comp: +~0.1 ms GPU (batched); measured 7.4 ms at batch=4 on CPU

risk.failure_mode: Logit averaging across members breaks the bit-exact streaming-equivalence gate unless the gate is extended to the ensemble.

candidates.confounds: Members must differ ONLY by seed, or this measures architectural diversity instead.
candidates.kill_criterion: N=3 does not beat the best single member by >0.15 WER pts.

candidates.name: Day-adversarial training via gradient reversal
candidates.mechanism: Attach a day classifier to the shared representation behind a gradient-reversal layer, forcing the encoder to produce day-invariant features while the day-specific affine layers absorb the day-specific part.
candidates.source: Ganin & Lempitsky DANN; not reported in any B2T writeup retrieved

dper.reasoning: The day-affine layers (26.7% of parameters) already provide an explicit, supervised mechanism for day adaptation, so an adversarial term is partly redundant.

latency.L_comp: 0 (discriminator dropped at inference)

risk.failure_mode: Adversarial training is unstable; the reversal coefficient needs a schedule.

candidates.confounds: Interacts with the day-layer learning rate group.
candidates.kill_criterion: No PER improvement, or training instability at any reversal coefficient.

candidates.name: Checkpoint averaging / SWA / model soup
candidates.mechanism: Average the weights of the last k validation checkpoints into one model. Zero inference cost - it produces a single model. AUDIT F8 shows best_val_PER is a minimum over 61 correlated evaluations and is ~0.04 pts optimistically biased, which is exactly the noise that weight averaging removes.
candidates.source: Izmailov et al. SWA; Wortsman et al. model soups

dper.reasoning: Late-training val PER has sd 0.033 pts across the last 10 evaluations (measured), so there is real variance to average away. Bounded because the checkpoints are highly correlated at the cosine LR floor.

latency.L_comp: 0 - single model at inference

risk.failure_mode: save_all_val_steps is FALSE (rnn_args.yaml:26), so no intermediate checkpoints exist. Costs one rerun to collect them - or is FREE if the flag is flipped on the next run that happens anyway.

candidates.confounds: Averaging across a LR schedule change is invalid; average only within the flat region.
candidates.kill_criterion: Averaged model does not beat the best single checkpoint on val PER.

candidates.name: Larger patch size (22 or 34) at unchanged stride
candidates.mechanism: Increase patch_size from 14 to 22 or 34 while holding patch_stride at 4. Each frame then integrates more past context at the SAME emission cadence, and because emission is right-edge, L_buf is unchanged. Only cold start grows - which BUDGET 2 shows is irrelevant here.
candidates.source: 7th-place B2T'25 used GRU variants at 34/4 and 22/4

dper.reasoning: A top-10 competition entry chose 22 and 34 over the baseline's 14, which is weak but real evidence that 14 is not optimal. Wairagkar's causal pipeline on this same participant integrates 1.5 s of past, far more than this repo's 280 ms patch.

latency.L_comp: patch embedding grows linearly: 34/14 = 2.4x on weight_ih_l0

candidates.memory: weight_ih_l0 grows from 16.5 M to 40 M params at P=34

risk.failure_mode: Changes the frame count and therefore adjusted_lens; short trials can hit adjusted_lens < target_lens -> infinite CTC loss -> crash.

candidates.confounds: Changes cold start (280 -> 680 ms) and parameter count simultaneously; report both.
candidates.kill_criterion: No PER improvement at P in {22, 34}.

candidates.name: Predictive distillation from a bidirectional teacher (S4)
candidates.mechanism: Train a bidirectional teacher, then distill into the causal student with a per-frame KD loss shifted by the teacher's measured emission delay, forcing the student to anticipate information the teacher only has in hindsight.
candidates.source: Reviewer prior S4; largely PRE-EMPTED by Delayed-KD arXiv:2505.22069 (non-streaming teacher -> streaming student via CTC posteriors, with a Temporal Alignment Buffer)

dper.reasoning: Doubly discounted. First, Delayed-KD already does this, and its Temporal Alignment Buffer already sweeps a delay range - S4's proposed differentiator (deriving the shift from measured peaks) is a narrow delta. Second, BUDGET 3 measures the causal/bidirectional emission offset at +4.64 ms, so there is almost no shift to apply.

latency.L_comp: 0 at inference (teacher discarded)

risk.failure_mode: Requires a bidirectional teacher run that is otherwise useless, and the KD weight/temperature interact with the CTC objective.

candidates.confounds: Distillation gain must be separated from the teacher simply being better.
candidates.kill_criterion: Student does not beat a same-cost directly-trained causal model.

candidates.name: Sweep smooth_kernel_std at fixed lookahead=0
candidates.mechanism: sigma=2 is inherited from the Willett-2023 lineage and has never been re-tuned for this model or for patch_size=14, which already integrates 14 bins. AUDIT F2 shows the accidental 37% bandwidth narrowing at L=0 coincided with the PER improvement, giving an evidence-backed direction.
candidates.source: AUDIT F2; Wairagkar et al. use a 1.5 s causal kernel on this participant - 15x longer than this repo's 100 ms

dper.reasoning: Directly motivated by an effect already observed in this project's own data. The direction is ambiguous though: the L=0 result argues for NARROWER, Wairagkar's 1.5 s kernel argues for much WIDER. Sweep both directions.

latency.L_comp: wider kernel = more past taps, still negligible

risk.failure_mode: A much wider causal kernel lengthens the streaming ring buffer; the equivalence gate must be re-run.

candidates.confounds: Must be run at fixed lookahead=0, and separately from bandwidth_matched_control (which changes the same kernel for a different purpose).
candidates.kill_criterion: No sigma in {1.0, 1.5, 3.0, 5.0} beats sigma=2 by >0.1 PER pts.

candidates.name: Lookahead convolution with k in {1,2}
candidates.mechanism: Insert a convolution that reads k future frames at a chosen depth, purchasing exactly 20k ms of L_algo in exchange for future context. Unlike smooth_lookahead, this is a clean, single-purpose lookahead knob that does not also change the smoothing bandwidth.
candidates.source: Deep Speech 2 lineage (no single modern citation retrieved - UNVERIFIED)

dper.reasoning: Modest gain per k. The real value is not accuracy: it is that this is the ONLY clean instrument for building a genuine accuracy-vs-lookahead curve, which AUDIT F2 shows the project currently lacks because smooth_lookahead confounds two variables.

latency.L_comp: +~1 MFLOP/frame

risk.failure_mode: Must be implemented so the streaming decoder genuinely waits for k frames, or the equivalence gate will pass while the deployed system cheats.

candidates.confounds: Changes L_algo, so it must be compared at matched total latency, not matched PER.
candidates.kill_criterion: PER improvement per k is under 0.1 pts, making the frontier flat in this instrument too.

candidates.name: Optimizer sweep: Adam epsilon, weight decay, LR schedule
candidates.mechanism: epsilon=0.1 is 10^7 times the PyTorch default of 1e-8, which largely disables Adam's adaptive term and makes it behave like signed SGD with momentum. weight_decay=0.001 is 5x lower than the 0.005 the 7th-place B2T'25 entry used. Both are inherited and untuned.
candidates.source: rnn_args.yaml:45-46; arXiv:2412.17227 explicitly credits LR-schedule tuning; 7th-place writeup

dper.reasoning: The '24 retrospective names LR scheduling as one of only two training changes that helped. eps=0.1 is extreme enough that it is either load-bearing or a fossil, and either answer is worth knowing.

risk.failure_mode: Lowering eps sharply may destabilize training given lr_max=0.005.

candidates.confounds: One variable per run.
candidates.kill_criterion: No config beats the baseline by >0.1 PER pts over 2 seeds.

candidates.name: Mixup and temporal warping
candidates.mechanism: Interpolate pairs of trials in feature space (mixup) and/or resample the time axis by a random factor (warping) to synthesize speaking-rate variation.
candidates.source: Standard; not reported in any B2T writeup retrieved

candidates.name: Causal rolling feature normalization (fixes AUDIT F1)
candidates.mechanism: Re-normalize the released features with a causal rolling estimator (Welford, ~10 s half-life) instead of the whole-block z-score the data actually carries, then retrain. AUDIT F1 establishes block normalization by a 1/sqrt(W) scaling test matching prediction within 1-26% across four sessions. Wairagkar et al. use exactly this rolling-past-10 s scheme in their real-time system on the SAME participant.
candidates.source: AUDIT F1 (measured); Wairagkar et al., Nature 644:145-152 (2025)

dper.reasoning: This is a COST, not a gain - the sign is deliberately positive. Removing a leak makes the task harder. The magnitude is the number the project needs and nobody has published: the true price of end-to-end causality on T15.

latency.L_comp: +negligible (Welford is O(1) per feature per bin)

risk.failure_mode: The exact upstream transform (clip before or after z-score) cannot be recovered from the released files, so the re-normalization is an approximation of an unknown original.

candidates.confounds: Must be run alone. Changes the input distribution, so every other tuned hyperparameter is potentially invalidated.
candidates.kill_criterion: Cannot be killed on accuracy grounds - a regression IS the result. Killed only if the rolling estimator cannot be made to reproduce the released features when given block statistics, indicating the transform was misidentified.
